from typing import List, Optional, Tuple


def wildcard_match(pattern: str, text: str) -> Optional[bool]:
    """ Match the whole of text against the glob pattern. Characters are
    Unicode code points and matching is case-sensitive. Pattern syntax:
      ?       matches exactly one character.
      *       matches any sequence of characters, including the empty one.
      [set]   matches exactly one character that is in the set; [!set]
              matches exactly one character that is not in the set. In a set,
              x-y is an inclusive range of code points; a ] that comes first
              (right after [ or [!) is a literal member; a - that comes first
              or last is a literal member; ^ and \\ have no special meaning.
      \\c      (backslash then any character c) matches c literally.
      any other character matches itself.
    The pattern is invalid if a [ has no closing ], if it ends in a lone
    backslash, or if a range has its start after its end (as in [z-a]); for an
    invalid pattern return None, whatever the text. Otherwise return True or
    False. Patterns and texts may be hundreds of characters long with many
    stars, so the running time must be polynomial (no exponential
    backtracking).
    >>> wildcard_match('*.py', 'main.py')
    True
    >>> wildcard_match('a[b', 'ab') is None
    True
    """
tests:
def check(candidate):
    assert candidate('a?c*', 'abcdef') is True
    assert candidate('', '') is True
    assert candidate('*', '') is True
    assert candidate('a*b*c', 'aXbYbZc') is True
    assert candidate('a*b*c', 'acb') is False
    assert candidate('[!a-c]x', 'bx') is False
    assert candidate('[]]', ']') is True
    assert candidate('[^a]', '^') is True
    assert candidate('\\*\\?[a-]', '*?-') is True
    assert candidate('a[b', 'ab') is None
    assert candidate('abc\\', 'abc') is None
    assert candidate('[z-a]', 'm') is None
    assert candidate('h?llo', 'héllo') is True
    assert candidate('*a*a*a*a*a*a*b', 'aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa') is False
    assert candidate('*a*a*a*a*a*a*a', 'aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa') is True

def test_check():
    check(wildcard_match)
solution:
from typing import List, Optional, Tuple


def wildcard_match(pattern: str, text: str) -> Optional[bool]:
    """ Match the whole of text against the glob pattern. Characters are
    Unicode code points and matching is case-sensitive. Pattern syntax:
      ?       matches exactly one character.
      *       matches any sequence of characters, including the empty one.
      [set]   matches exactly one character that is in the set; [!set]
              matches exactly one character that is not in the set. In a set,
              x-y is an inclusive range of code points; a ] that comes first
              (right after [ or [!) is a literal member; a - that comes first
              or last is a literal member; ^ and \\ have no special meaning.
      \\c      (backslash then any character c) matches c literally.
      any other character matches itself.
    The pattern is invalid if a [ has no closing ], if it ends in a lone
    backslash, or if a range has its start after its end (as in [z-a]); for an
    invalid pattern return None, whatever the text. Otherwise return True or
    False. Patterns and texts may be hundreds of characters long with many
    stars, so the running time must be polynomial (no exponential
    backtracking).
    >>> wildcard_match('*.py', 'main.py')
    True
    >>> wildcard_match('a[b', 'ab') is None
    True
    """
    tokens = _parse(pattern)
    if tokens is None:
        return None
    t = list(text)
    p, i = 0, 0
    star, star_i = -1, 0
    while i < len(t):
        if p < len(tokens) and tokens[p][0] != '*' and _one(tokens[p], t[i]):
            p += 1
            i += 1
        elif p < len(tokens) and tokens[p][0] == '*':
            star, star_i = p, i
            p += 1
        elif star >= 0:
            # let the last star absorb one more character and retry
            star_i += 1
            p, i = star + 1, star_i
        else:
            return False
    while p < len(tokens) and tokens[p][0] == '*':
        p += 1
    return p == len(tokens)


def _one(tok, c: str) -> bool:
    kind = tok[0]
    if kind == '?':
        return True
    if kind == 'lit':
        return tok[1] == c
    inside = any(lo <= c <= hi for lo, hi in tok[2])
    return inside != tok[1]


def _parse(pattern: str):
    """Tokens ('*',), ('?',), ('lit', c), ('set', negated, [(lo, hi)]), or None."""
    p = list(pattern)
    out = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(p):
        c = p[i]
        if c == '*' or c == '?':
            out.append((c,))
            i += 1
        elif c == '\\':
            if i + 1 >= len(p):
                return None
            out.append(('lit', p[i + 1]))
            i += 2
        elif c == '[':
            j = i + 1
            neg = j < len(p) and p[j] == '!'
            if neg:
                j += 1
            items: List[Tuple[str, str]] = []
            first = True
            while True:
                if j >= len(p):
                    return None
                if p[j] == ']' and not first:
                    break
                first = False
                if j + 2 < len(p) and p[j + 1] == '-' and p[j + 2] != ']':
                    if p[j] > p[j + 2]:
                        return None
                    items.append((p[j], p[j + 2]))
                    j += 3
                else:
                    items.append((p[j], p[j]))
                    j += 1
            out.append(('set', neg, items))
            i = j + 1
        else:
            out.append(('lit', c))
            i += 1
    return out
